Proverbs 30:4.bridge: The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh begin here.

Isaiah 7:7.bridge: Syria and the northern kingdom of Israel plot to invade Judah and set their own puppet king on its throne.

Isaiah 20:2.bridge: When an Assyrian general captures the Philistine city of Ashdod, God gives Isaiah an acted sign about Egypt and Ethiopia, which Judah hoped would protect it.

Isaiah 21:9.bridge: In a vision about Babylon, Isaiah posts a watchman to report whatever approaches; at last riders come with news.

Isaiah 22:12.bridge: Isaiah turns to Jerusalem, which in a crisis fortifies its walls and stores water but never looks to God.

Isaiah 22:20.bridge: God sends Isaiah to Shebna, the royal steward who is carving himself a grand tomb, to tell him he will be thrown out of office.
